speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual presentation; have you noticed any specific triggers, such as flashing lights, strong smells, or emotional stress, before these episodes of unresponsiveness? Also, do you experience any warning sensations like a rising stomach feeling or visual distortions immediately before?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Seizures with secondary generalization (likely evolving into complex partial or atypical absence seizures given the duration and motor components).

I need to confirm if these events occur during sleep and if there is a family history of epilepsy to differentiate this from other non-epileptic causes. Please also provide an EEG report if one has been done. REQUEST TEST: EEG; REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI.
